answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation earned only through verified work: an agent's trust grows slowly, like yarrow spreading roots, and the plume of its past deeds becomes its proof. Newcomers with no history get only tiny, low-value tasks until peers attest their results. A falcon-eyed grader then spot-checks random outputs, so spinning up a thousand empty identities buys nothing — every fake must pay the same slow cost of earning trust as a real agent.
